surf_collections_strings: hash rows added 2026-11-16 (SF-1 dth_*, SF-2 dec_*)

Rows dth_* come from the native Datetime, Time and Date hashCode capture and
rows dec_* from the Decimal hashCode capture. Both ran in scratch orgs at API
62.0 and 67.0, two repeats each; the repeats agree. Every outcome is the
unmodified test-result message (or the compile problem, or the queried log
payload) from raw/. The cases are Class.method in cases.tsv; the harness runs
each captured method alone.

Source restorations: the capture scrubbed the DthTz user emails and usernames
to a placeholder; they are synthetic example.invalid addresses here. The Dec
capture parked anonymous payloads in a Dec_Log__c record; the anonymous
sources print the same payload with System.debug. The Dec_Hash_Access
permission set was an environment step in the capture (assigned to the
running user, glade.yml replays it); Dth_Probe_Access is assigned only to the
runAs users, as in the capture, so the API 67.0 DthField insert is the native
"fields being inaccessible" DmlException.

Volatile values: the Datetime rows that read an inserted record's CreatedDate
(the S, SOQL, FM and FR tails) hold the clock. The harness masks those tails
after checking that each hash is Long.hashCode(ms) XOR 577755.

Fixes these rows drove: Julian civil dates before 1582-10-15 in the Datetime
builders; real offset history for America/Los_Angeles, Asia/Kolkata and
Australia/Adelaide before 2008; the 1700-01-01..4000-12-31 DateTime field
range on insert; List<Decimal> == by scale; Percent and Number integer-part
overflow on insert with the API 62 and API 67 wording; Time.getTime and
Date.getTime as compile errors. hashCode itself already matched.

Not observed, so base behavior: the cross-type direct hash grid and the rest below.
The cross-type direct hash grid for Double, Long and
Integer covers 1.5d, 1 and 1 only. DecHashWrap did not compile natively and
has no row. Currency overflow, rounding-edge overflow, Julian readers
(yearGmt and formatGmt of a pre-cutover instant) are not captured; the readers
read the same Julian civil date the builders were given, so one civil input
round-trips (neighbor test), and Datetime.parse and the local valueOf build
Julian too. Other zones' history is unobserved.

dth_loc_* rows (SF-1b, 2026-11-16): the locale capture, API 62.0 and 67.0, test
and anonymous, repeats agree (test r1 and r3 compared). A Datetime keeps the
hash of its construction: built under en_US and hashed in a de runAs it stays
577755, and the reverse stays 577677. Language-only de and fr hash as Mon/4
(577677). is_IS, nl_NL and de_DE are Mon/4, fa_IR Sat/1 (577751), iw_IL and es_MX
Sun/1 (577755), tr_TR Mon/1 (577757). dv_MV and he_IL are rejected by the
LocaleSidKey picklist. Date and Time hashes carry no week term; List, Set and Map
follow the element hashes. The anonymous rows run as a user of that locale
(cases.tsv column 4).

Fixes: a Datetime value stamps the user's week term the first time an expression
yields it; its hash uses the stamp. A Datetime produced from a stamped one
(addDays and the like) keeps the source's term; no native row covers arithmetic,
so that is a choice. A Datetime read from an SObject field, a SOQL row or JSON is
stamped when an expression first yields it, not when the query ran; SObject
field hashes still read the locale at hash time. A language-only locale maps to
its CLDR likely region (table in platform_sobject_members.go); only de and fr are
captured. de, fr and fa_IR are accepted as test locale keys. The Maldives
(MV) term is still unobserved, because dv_MV is rejected.

dth_r2_* rows (second batch, 2026-11-17, API 62.0 and 67.0, two repeats, one
scratch org per repeat, deleted and verified): DateTime and Date field range
(insert, Database.insert and update: 1700-01-01 through 4000-12-31, rejected with
FIELD_INTEGRITY_EXCEPTION naming the value); Decimal collection equality (List ==,
equals, contains, indexOf, List<Object>, nested lists, a Set and a record's
Decimal field all compare scale: 1.5 differs from 1.50, 3 from 3.0); time-zone
display (format z and zzzz, getOffset and the label follow the zone's real
history for LA, Adelaide and Kolkata); PageReference text (every text form is
System.PageReference[url]; JSON.serialize throws; the unset current page is
System.PageReference[null]; new PageReference() does not exist natively); the
SF-1b stamping shapes across users (SOQL, JSON, record field, list, map, valueOf,
addDays).
Masked in the harness: TimeZone.getDisplayName names the zone at the moment of
the run, so tzdisp drops it; record ids in update messages.
Left as base: the hash of a whole SObject (it includes the Id), UserRecordAccess
beyond the three sharing models below, and the Maldives term.

Raw for the dth_r2_* rows: the campaign evidence directory parallel/batch2-20261117 (README.txt names the run
directory of each class). The dth_r3_* rows come from the same directory: cap5_r1 and cap5_r2
(CalShapes, CalArith, CalDate, pgctor, pgctor_ok) and cap6_r1 and cap6_r2 (CalLocal2, CalParse).

dth_r3_* rows (third batch, 2026-11-17, API 62.0 and 67.0, two repeats): the hybrid calendar. A Date before
1582-10-15 is a Julian civil date (1500-02-29 exists; Date 1500-01-01 hashes as the real instant and
serializes as 1500-01-10); a Datetime keeps its real instant, and every reader (valueOf in the user's
zone, concatenation and toString in GMT, year/month/day/dayOfYear, date, format) reads the Julian civil
date, while JSON.serialize writes the proleptic Gregorian text. addMonths and addYears work on the civil
date and clamp to the month's own length (Julian 1400-02-29 plus a year is 1401-02-28). The Date members
addDays, addMonths, addYears, daysBetween, dayOfYear, toStartOfWeek, daysInMonth and isLeapYear follow
the same calendar. Year 1 is Julian; years before 1 stay proleptic (uncaptured). Datetime.parse and
Date.parse read no date before 1700 (Invalid date/time), and valueOf reads any year. Before a zone's
first recorded transition (Los Angeles before 1883) the offset is the standard one and formatLong names
it GMT-8. pgctor: new PageReference() fails to compile natively; pgctor_ok: System.debug of a
PageReference prints System.PageReference[url]. JSON.deserialize of a Date reads the Gregorian date and
keeps it as the Julian label of the same instant, so its JSON text round-trips.
Typed flow merges (FlowTyped, cap5): a String assignment that merges a Number variable or formula renders
the declared scale (2.50, 7.00), a Date renders as January 2, 2026, a Boolean as true, and a String as is,
alone or inside text; native rejects such a merge into a Number, Boolean or Date variable at deploy time
(flow-target-reject raw; an automation test pins the message). Glade matches all of that. Uncaptured, so on
the earlier behavior: Currency, DateTime and other resource types, and a Number without a declared scale.
The flow change is gated to autolaunched flows and a String target.
dth_r3_fmtjulian (cap7): format() on Julian dates. The weekday, day of year, week of year, week of month,
day of week in month and year tokens, and formatLong, follow the hybrid calendar (1500-02-29 is a Saturday,
day 60, week 9). The weekday-name and weekday-number tokens read English only; other locales keep the label
shifted reading for those two tokens.
